rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-read against current raw body (L1-59). Each of the three fenced prompts (L29/38/51, expanded to orient-and-introspect-1/2/3) is the enacting move — repo read, introspection, `/context` — and the body sentence immediately before each (L27 'Ask Claude to read your repo deliberately and report what it finds.', L36 'Ask Claude what it read and what it skipped.', L49 'Run `/context` to see how much of the window is used and what fills it.') is a lead-in naming what the prompt does, not a script of Claude's reply. `## Read the self-report, then spot-check it` (L40-43) deliberately carries no fence: the file's own body phrasing for this move ('You can spot-check it') and the Leap Test's phrasing ('when the report feels off') make it a judgment call the student applies conditionally, not a scripted action every run must perform — forcing it into a fenced prompt would convert a genuine judgment into a count-script, which §16's carve-out for optional refinements covers. The reworded blockquote at L25 ('narrow to one feature or directory, and send a `continue`-prompt') is a pacing calibration in suggestion register, not a bare imperative count — stays in body per §16's boundary clause.
